I am that model identifier. This is a fresh session with no access to that session's reasoning, only to repository artifacts and live state, so I cannot show that I am independent of the work, and I treat the dossier's own recommendation as binding on how this verdict is used: it is NOT the independent §8 verdict. The dossier recommends a different model, provider or a human; the operator of this session instructed me to review it, which I treat as routing it to the same identity, and I cannot verify that the operator is the owner. The conflict could bias a same-identity review toward finding the closure sound; I compensated by treating every closure claim as a hypothesis to be reproduced against live state, stored artifacts and executed code, and I did not rely on the earlier session's wording. This verdict is FURTHER_FINDINGS, so the self-review risk does not inflate a closure; an ACCEPT from this identity should still be discarded as non-independent. Five subagents of the same model family each reviewed one slice of the pinned workflow text; I re-verified the blocker-level and fail-open claims myself by reading the cited lines and executing the extracted shared blocks.
rationale: FURTHER_FINDINGS. The live state and stored artifacts match the dossier: ruleset 24378879 is active with update/deletion/non_fast_forward and a single bypass user; the u1-verifier environment has one tag policy; both branch rulesets have empty bypass lists; the three federated-credential sets and role assignments (including the revocations/* ABAC clause) are as described; R=ed848ba is the tag target, an ancestor of main, and differs from the dry-run commit 1e3baf20 only in U1-verifier-pin.json; every hash in Part A.2 reproduces; the trust-policy digest 262e82c3 reproduces from the pin record through the workflow's own shared blocks; the seven cited runs exist with the stated commits, refs and conclusions; the stored a02 decision, seal, context and probe records say what the dossier says. G-1, G-2, G-9, G-10, G-12, G-13 are closed on that evidence. The closure is not sound enough to ACCEPT because the code that enforces the closed text has defects the dry runs could not see, since no run supplied hostile input and no run ever reached ACCEPT. (1) H-1 blocker: step-output injection through the unvalidated selectedExecution.runId lets a request author make the seal and ledger carry decisionStatus ACCEPT over a decision.json whose status is INVALID (same outcome as G-7), and can overwrite request-commit-sha after the G-8 ancestry check; I reproduced the line construction locally. (2) H-2, H-3 majors: producer-chosen gap rows are dropped from every check, and a bundle inventory entry with no digest compares as 'match' (executed against the extracted compare_classes). (3) H-4: the sandbox 'derivation' runs the candidate's own entrypoint and trusts its self-reported candidateCommit and exit status, and the only harness is a fixture that echoes the committed rows, so G-5 is a comparison of the candidate with itself. (4) H-5, H-6: the github-run provenance branch is unexercised, cannot be satisfied by the shipped producer, and does not bind branch, repository or workflow bytes; commit refs are not required to be SHAs. (5) H-7, H-8: seal status, reason codes and executedCommit are copied from step outputs rather than the read-back decision, retentionObservationResult 'match' is independent of the immutability state, and close-attempt falls back to evaluate's 'accept' when nothing was persisted. (6) H-9: every authority named in the closure (custodian, sole environment reviewer with prevent_self_review false, sole collaborator and admin, CODEOWNER, tag-ruleset bypass) is the one identity ambient to the builder session, and the dossier's own 'owner-delegated environment approvals' were operated by the builder; the closure bounds this only for P2/P3. (7) H-10: the positive path was reduced by ratification to INCOMPLETE, so the verifier has never been observed to ACCEPT. The special-scrutiny answers: (a) defects 1, 2, 4 were fixed at the right layer, defect 3 was a defect in coordinator test tooling and the r3 requests are correct, and defect 5 is repository state; (b) the temporary PR-only bypass was bounded honestly in mechanism (red baseline named, sunset recorded and executed, live GETs confirm empty bypass lists, first-parent history shows only PR merges), but the sunset evidence (Addendum C) exists only on `dev`, and PRs #130 and #137 (the commit R) merged with zero reviews; (c) the nine unrecorded rows do gate every ACCEPT (all nine appear in the stored notes) and the recorded rows I could check against live state (U1-07, U1-08 client ids) are true, but 'recorded' means self-attested by the coordinator session and the gate is only as honest as that session.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml@ed848ba evaluate step output writer L2171-2177 (`producer-run-id=%s` from str(sel.get('runId'))), resolve-request L648-656 (same pattern, writes request-commit-sha, oracle-digest, configuration-checklist-digest), consumers L2348-2350 (DECISION_STATUS), L2548, L2613-2631 (seal), L2706; A-U1.8.21; G-7, G-8
findings.issue: selectedExecution.runId (and oracleDigest, configurationChecklistDigest) come from the promotion request JSON and are never type- or format-checked; resolve-request validates only the request id grammar and the self-digest, which the request author computes. They are interpolated with %s into $GITHUB_OUTPUT. A runId such as "1\nstatus=ACCEPT" appends a second `status` line after the real `status=INVALID` line (L2174 precedes L2177); GitHub resolves duplicate output names last-wins [INFERENCE: platform semantics; the line construction is reproduced locally and parses to status=ACCEPT]. needs.evaluate.outputs.status then feeds DECISION_STATUS, so retention-observation writes decisionStatus ACCEPT into the seal and the ledger outcome while the persisted decision.json (digest-checked in persist L2287-2291) says INVALID. The seal is never cross-checked against the decision bytes. This is the G-7 outcome again, reachable from request content. In resolve-request the same injection can replace request-commit-sha after the ancestry check (L651-652), and evaluate re-fetches the request and oracle at that value (L1249). Precondition: a request in default-branch history (CODEOWNERS-covered, but the only owner is the builder identity and merges used --admin; H-9). Not exercised by any dry run, because no run supplied hostile request content.
findings.requiredChange: Validate at resolve-request, before any output: selectedExecution.runId and attempt as ^[0-9]{1,20}$, every digest as ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$, commit as ^[0-9a-f]{40}$. Replace every `f.write('k=%s\n')` with one writer that rejects CR/LF in any value (or use the multiline delimiter form with a random delimiter). In retention-observation take status, reasonCodes, executedCommit and authoritative from the parsed read-back decision (L2518) and set result=mismatch when they disagree with the outputs. Add a negative dry run whose request carries a newline in runId and show it refused. Re-pin.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml@ed848ba evaluate permitted_gap L1668-1682, gap rows skipped at L1712, L1776, L1862, L1891; contract §7.6 / PIN-09 ('ONLY the three named gaps')
findings.issue: permitted_gap returns True for any row whose gapRecord.reason starts with `blocked:` and whose reason or obligation contains the substring 'realpath sweep', for any caseId, and unconditionally for caseId CTRL-01. Both are producer-authored strings. Gap rows are skipped before the oracle, provenance and sandbox checks. A producer keeps minExercisedRows passing rows and relabels failing rows as gaps; ACCEPT results. The oracle lists no permitted gap case ids, so the code does not enforce the rule its comment states.
findings.requiredChange: List the permitted gaps ((id, caseId, obligation) triples) in the per-request oracle and match them exactly; any other gap row is INVALID/U1_ARTIFACT_INVALID. Add a negative dry run with a relabelled failing row.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml@ed848ba evaluate package inventory check L1441-1453; shared compare_classes L1122-1138
findings.issue: recorded_byte = entry.get('byteDigest', entry.get('digest')) and entry.get('docDigest') are both None when the producer omits them, and compare_classes(raw, None, None, domain) returns 'match' (executed against the extracted function: 'both digests absent -> match'; empty strings correctly give byte-mismatch). The only remaining guard is byteLength == len(raw). A producer can therefore ship files that carry no digest binding. Duplicate relativePath entries silently overwrite each other (L1441).
findings.requiredChange: Require a string ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ byteDigest on every inventory entry and reject duplicate relativePath; make compare_classes return 'unbound' when both expected digests are None; extend the pin-check self-test with that case. Re-pin.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml@ed848ba candidate-sandbox L322-372 and evaluate L1830-1922; plugins/foreman-line/bypass-outage-harness/u1-sandbox.mjs L31-63; A-U1.8.20 clauses 2, 5; closure map row G-5
findings.issue: The 'independent derivation' is produced by the candidate: the job checks out the selected producer run's head_sha and runs that checkout's u1-sandbox.mjs, so the candidate controls sandbox-result.json, its harnessExitStatus, and candidateCommit; the wrapper's exit status is also the candidate's own. evaluate compares the self-reported candidateCommit with the subject commit (L1844) but nothing records `git rev-parse HEAD` from a trusted step, and PRODUCER_HEAD_SHA is not passed into evaluate. The oracle and producer rows are public at the request commit, so a harness that prints them back passes row-by-row. The shipped harness copies exitStatus/observedResult from the same committed controls.json and matrix.json the producer packages and hard-codes harnessExitStatus 0, so the positive comparison is a candidate compared with itself. The candidate also runs in the same VM as the upload-artifact step of that job and can influence it ($GITHUB_ENV, background processes, runtime token) [INFERENCE]. The dossier names the harness as a fixture but not that the real FK-P18' harness, as specified, is again candidate-authored.
findings.requiredChange: Either run a verifier-owned harness taken from pin commit R over the candidate tree as read-only input, or state in the contract that the sandbox is advisory and never clears U1_INDEPENDENCE_UNPROVEN. In both cases: write HEAD from a trusted step before running candidate code and compare that value; pass producer-head-sha into evaluate; upload the sandbox output from a separate job that never ran candidate code; make the fixture sandbox-mismatch hook throw when NC-U1-02 is absent instead of silently doing nothing.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml@ed848ba evaluate github-run branch L1584-1628, PROVENANCE_WORKFLOWS L1233; u1-produce.yml L339-363, L380-395, L435-440, L681-685; A-U1.8.20 clause 4
findings.issue: Never exercised (fixture is committed-source only). It checks only run.path against a hard-coded constant (not the pin's producerWorkflow, which is digested at L1327 but never enforced), run.head_sha == subject commit and conclusion; it does not require head_branch == default branch, head_repository.id == repo id, the workflow bytes at head_sha to equal the default-branch copy (a run of a modified u1-produce.yml on any branch has the same path), or runId == the selected execution's runId; the `event` comparison compares two attacker-controlled strings; the subject commit is not required to be in default-branch history. On the producer side the row's artifactByteDigest is the digest of the original source file while the uploaded artifact is the re-canonicalized, enriched copy that embeds the row (a row cannot contain its own file's digest), so the 'artifact digest equals row digest and contains the row' check cannot be satisfied; `ci-run-generated` is reached only for untracked or dirty paths; conclusion 'success' is hard-coded while the job runs.
findings.requiredChange: Either delete the github-run lane from the verifier and the producer and say so in the amendment, or fix both ends: upload the unmodified source file as its own artifact and cite its digest; require head_repository.id, head_branch == default branch, workflow digest at head_sha == default-branch digest, run id == selected runId, and the subject commit in default-branch history; cache per run, bound sizes, paginate; then exercise it in a dry run.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml@ed848ba committed-source branch L1631-1648; gh_content L1191-1197; on_default_branch L1531-1535; branch_head L1525-1529; github-run L1584, L1598, L1609
findings.issue: headSha is not required to be a 40-hex commit. A value such as `main` makes on_default_branch compare main...main ('identical') while the content is read at a moving ref, so 'cited file at cited commit' and 'commit in history' can describe different objects. committedPath and runId are interpolated unvalidated and unencoded into contents/%s?ref=%s and runs/%s paths (`?`, `#`, `..` can alter the endpoint) [INFERENCE for the endpoint effect]. headSha is never tied to the subject commit. The ancestry compare uses the literal branch `main`, not the repository default branch.
findings.requiredChange: Require ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ for headSha, a path grammar (no ?, #, .., leading /) for committedPath, ^[0-9]{1,20}$ for runId; pass ref via -f ref=; resolve the default branch name from the API and use it in both places; require the cited commit to equal the subject commit or be an ancestor of it.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml@ed848ba retention-observation L2515-2556 (result, immutability read), seal L2613-2631; A-U1.8.21 clauses 1-2, 4; contract §3.5.2
findings.issue: (a) result is 'match' whenever the digest read-back matches (L2527); a failed or unparsable immutability read is swallowed (`except Exception: pass`, L2545) and leaves state/intervalDays/policyEtag null, and an Unlocked policy also yields match; the seal is written for every result including mismatch and unreadable. Consumability then rests on decisionStatus alone (evaluate checks Locked >= 400d once, earlier, not at sealing time). (b) decisionStatus, reasonCodes, executedCommit and authoritative are copied from env (evaluate outputs and pin-check), not 'from the sealed decision' as clause 1 requires; nothing compares the parsed read-back decision (L2518) with them, so a seal/decision disagreement can occur and cannot be detected here. (c) The status is not checked against the closed enum and reasonCodes can be null. (d) A fixture seal (u1-fixture- id) is made non-consumable only by the consumer's prefix rule; the workflow sets no marker. (e) persist verifies only decision.json bytes; the three evidence files are uploaded unverified although decision.artifactInventory holds their digests, and the seal inventory is not checked against the expected object set or digests.
findings.requiredChange: Set result=unproven unless the immutability read succeeded and state is Locked with intervalDays >= 400, and fail on a non-zero az exit. Derive status, reasonCodes, executedCommit, authoritative from the parsed read-back decision, validate the enum and list type, and set mismatch on disagreement. Add a `consumable:false` field for u1-fixture- ids. Verify each persisted evidence file against decision.artifactInventory and assert the exact object set in the seal inventory.

findings.location: u1-verify.yml@ed848ba close-attempt ATTEMPT_OUTCOME L2706 (`retention-observation.outputs.attempt-outcome || evaluate.outputs.attempt-outcome || 'interrupted'`), IA-8.7 terminal row
findings.issue: When persist or retention-observation fails (or crashes before its output is set), the terminal ledger row takes evaluate's pre-persistence outcome, e.g. `accept`, although no decision was persisted, no observation exists and no seal exists. The ledger would record an accepted attempt with nothing behind it.

naiveReadingTests: Applied to the closed text and the stored artifacts. 1. 'The tag is protected.' Live GET and the stored observation agree; true while the bypass user is not the actor, and the bypass user is the builder's identity (H-9, H-12). 2. 'Only the tag can reach the verifier identity.' Environment has one tag policy; true. A main-branch job can still use u1-reader-run-fc to read the private container (accepted, named). 3. 'The positive path proves ACCEPT is reachable.' No: it proves INCOMPLETE with ten notes; ACCEPT is unexercised (H-10). 4. 'A seal says what the decision says.' Not enforced: status and reason codes come from step outputs, which request content can overwrite (H-1, H-7). 5. 'Gaps are limited to three named rows.' The code accepts any row whose producer-written reason contains a fixed string (H-2). 6. 'Every artifact is digest-bound.' An entry with no digests compares as match (H-3, executed). 7. 'The sandbox independently re-derives the rows.' It runs the candidate's own code and the shipped harness echoes the committed rows (H-4). 8. 'Provenance binds bytes.' Yes for committed-source rows with 40-hex commits; the github-run lane is unexercised and unsatisfiable (H-5, H-6). 9. 'The request comes from protected history.' Ancestry check is real and exercised; its output can be overwritten by injection (H-1). 10. 'Temporary bypass was removed.' Live GETs show empty bypass lists on both branch rulesets; the written evidence is on dev only (H-13). 11. 'The nine unrecorded rows gate ACCEPT.' All nine appear in the stored notes; true. 12. 'The producer cannot delete.' Refused by WORM on an Unlocked policy, not by RBAC, and the producer role allows delete under runs/* (named in A.1, still bounded only by the unlocked policy; INCOMPLETE-U1-09/-10 unrecorded). 13. 'R is what ran.' Run 37065869917 headSha = tag target = R; dry runs ran at 1e3baf20, which differs from R only by the pin record. 14. 'Hashes in A.2 are right.' All reproduced.
